#### What type of PR is this?

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Add the file reading and writing test case into e2e GMSA tests. In this test case, the pod with GMSACredentialSpec should be able to read and write files from/to the remote folder in Active Directory server.

The assumptions of this test case are:
-  all the assumptions of the existing "works end to end" test case 
- there should be a folder created on Active Directory server and shared with the expected gMSA user.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/100388

review_comments: any reason this is in eventually and the write above isn't? Should these be separate pods to ensure we aren't doing anything funny with writing to local paths?

Thanks for the advice! I updated the code and moved the write into the eventually function. 
Also I added a comment to the filepath variable to tell folks not to change it. "gmsaSharedFolder" variable can be changed to other folder, but as long as the "filePath" variable(line229) doesn't change in their pr, it would still be a remote folder and the test takes effect. Do you think it's good enough to prevent writing to local paths?
yes I think this makes sense.

Is there any reason we are using the IP address here instead of the dns name of the doman controller?  We had an issue in the past where there was a bug with the DNS name but ip worked fine: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa/issues/30.

Yeah, thanks for pointing this out. I'm using AD 2016 so dns name doesn't work for me. I tried the fix mentioned in the issue but it broke my testbed. I'll spend more time on this and follow up on the refactor pr.
All of this logic is the same as the `GMSA support` logic. Can we hoist this to a `before` clause that will set up the cluster with the web hook once (and do the clean up in a `after`)?
That's a good point! I'm planning to merge this one first and create another pr to do the refactor so that this pr won't be messed up. Does it make sense to you?
can you create an issue to track this clean up.  I think it is important clean up to be done but could be a good first issue
Sure, I created it and assigned to myself. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108649
